routes.label: Multiply the successive fractions of pie remaining

question: Harold made a plum pie to take on a picnic. He was able to eat only \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the pie, and he left the rest for his friends. A moose came by and ate \(\frac{1}{3}\) of what Harold left behind. After that, a porcupine ate \(\frac{1}{3}\) of what the moose left behind. How much of the original pie still remained after the porcupine left?
solution:
Each animal eats a fraction of the pie that is left at that moment. It is convenient to track the fraction remaining after each step.

Harold leaves \(1-\frac14=\frac34\) of the original pie. The moose eats one third of that remainder, so it leaves two thirds of it. The porcupine then also leaves two thirds of the new remainder. Thus the fraction of the original pie still present is

\[
\frac34\cdot\frac23\cdot\frac23=\frac13.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac13}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\). Multiplying the successive fractions remaining keeps track of the changing whole.

nodes.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number , e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?
nodes.label: 4.NF.B.4c

nodes.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b. For example, use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) × 4 = 8/3, and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15. (In general, (a/b) × (c/d) = ac/bd.)

edges.reason: The integer-multiplier case supplies a useful stepping stone and repeated-addition interpretation. The product-of-numerators/product-of-denominators rule follows directly from a part-of-a-part area model without executing the earlier decimal-free integer-multiplier procedure; Gemini confuses this customary progression with necessity.

The endpoint provides explicit quantity-modeling experience that can help translate a fraction-of-a-whole story into an expression. Price and speed formulas do not define a fractional part, so the benefit is preparation only. This final scoped judgment does not treat a prior native acceptance of Claude's rejection as an accepted dependency.
